$comment: Golden inputs for the cache-key algorithm (rules/cache-key.md). Both implementations load this and assert build_cache_key(qualname, args, kwargs) == expected.

examples.name: unicode-arg-stays-utf8
examples.$comment: Non-ASCII characters are written as UTF-8, never as \uXXXX escapes.

examples.name: html-chars-not-escaped
examples.$comment: <, > and & are written literally (no \u003c-style HTML escaping), in values and in object keys.

examples.name: control-and-separator-chars
examples.$comment: Short escapes for \n and \t, \u00XX (lowercase hex) for other C0 controls, and U+2028 written literally.

examples.name: object-keys-sorted-by-code-point
examples.$comment: Object keys sort by Unicode code point (same order as their UTF-8 bytes), not by UTF-16 code unit: U+FF5E sorts before the astral U+1F600, although the emoji's leading surrogate (0xD83D) is the smaller code unit.

examples.name: long-key-hashed
examples.$comment: When the raw key exceeds 250 UTF-8 bytes, the parens content is replaced with sha256:<hex>. Test asserts that the prefix matches and the raw key would have been over 250 bytes; the exact hex is implementation-derived and computed at test time, NOT hard-coded here.
